calls.head: Colorado’s shot volume meets a soft spot
calls.body: Winnipeg is 22nd of 32 at shot suppression, and Colorado is one of the league’s busiest shooting teams (1st: 69.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5).
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Colorado took 69.4 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against its usual 69.6.

calls.head: Two of the league’s busiest games meet
calls.body: Colorado’s games average 88.2 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (1st of 32 for pace); Winnipeg’s average 83.2 (10th).
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 94.8 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 85.7 and a league average of 81.7.

WPG.head: We gave Winnipeg a 36% chance, and Winnipeg proved us wrong.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 64% chance, but Winnipeg had other ideas.

surprises.head: Winnipeg won without the better chances
surprises.body: Expected goals favoured Colorado, 2.9 to 2.0, with empty nets left out.

surprises.head: Winnipeg tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Iafallo, A. Lowry, M. Barron played 11:01 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Winnipeg’s usual lines.
